memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised, and his son Ishmael was thirteen; Abraham and his son Ishmael were both circumcised on that same day. And every male in Abraham's household, including those born in his household or bought from a foreigner, were circumcised with him. - Gen 17:24-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Ninety-nine years old, and Abraham submits to the painful, humbling sign of the covenant. He could have pleaded his age, his standing, his comfort. Instead, the old man obeys - and his whole household obeys with him. Ishmael at thirteen, the servants, the foreigners bought into the family, every single male. No one was excused, least of all Abraham himself.

There is real dignity in this picture. Abraham does not ask his household to do anything he won't do first. He leads by example, bearing the sign in his own aged body before requiring it of anyone else. That is godly leadership - going first, not merely commanding others.

And notice again: it is never too late to obey God. At ninety-nine, Abraham is still learning, still submitting, still stepping into new obedience. Some imagine that a certain age or stage exempts them from fresh obedience to God. Abraham shows otherwise. Until our last breath, God may call us to new steps of faith.

Whatever your age or season, God is not finished with you. He called Abraham to a costly obedience at ninety-nine and honoured it. The chapter closes with a whole household marked as God's own, because one old man obeyed. "Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength" (Isa 40:31). Step forward in obedience, whatever your age. God still has purposes for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you think you're too old or too settled for new obedience to God?
- Are you leading those around you by going first?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that I am never too old or too settled to obey You. Give me the humility of Abraham, to go first and to keep stepping into new obedience whatever my age. You are not finished with me yet.
Amen.
